slide_title: The Human Cardiovascular System: Heartbeat & Cardiac Cycle
original_text: The Human Cardiovascular System Heartbeat Systole-Contraction of heart chambers Diastole-Relaxation of heart chambers Cardiac cycle -Two-part pumping action that takes about a second Blood collects in atria, the atria contract Pushes blood through tricuspid and mitral valves into the resting lower ventricles AtrioleSystole, Ventricular Diastole Second part begins after the ventricles fill Ventricles contract AV valves close, Semilunar valves open Lubsound AtrioleDiastole, Ventricular Systole After blood moves into the pulmonary artery and aorta, the ventricles relax Semilunar valves close Dub sound
explanation: The heartbeat is regulated by the cardiac cycle, which consists of systole (contraction of heart chambers) and diastole (relaxation of heart chambers). This cycle is a two-part pumping action lasting about one second: 1) Atrial Systole, Ventricular Diastole: Blood collects in the atria, which contract, pushing blood through the tricuspid and mitral (bicuspid) valves into the relaxed ventricles. 2) Atrial Diastole, Ventricular Systole: Once the ventricles fill, they contract. The sudden pressure closes the AV valves (producing the 'lub' sound) and opens the semilunar valves. 3) Ventricular Diastole: As blood enters the pulmonary trunk and aorta, the ventricles relax, and the semilunar valves snap shut to prevent backflow, producing the 'dub' sound.

questions.q: What event is responsible for generating the 'lub' sound of the heartbeat?
opts: The closure of the atrioventricular (AV) valves during ventricular systole
The closure of the semilunar valves during ventricular diastole
The flow of blood through the capillary beds
questions.exp: The first heart sound ('lub') is caused by the snapping shut of the atrioventricular (tricuspid and mitral) valves when the ventricles contract during ventricular systole.

questions.q: What occurs during the second part of the cardiac cycle when the ventricles contract?
opts: Closure of the semilunar valves and opening of the AV valves
Both atria and ventricles relax simultaneously
questions.exp: When the ventricles contract (ventricular systole), the atria are relaxed (atrial diastole).

questions.q: What causes the 'dub' sound of the heartbeat?
opts: The opening of the AV valves
The closing of the semilunar valves during ventricular diastole
The passage of blood through the venae cavae
The electrical charging of the SA node
questions.exp: The second heart sound ('dub') is produced by the closure of the semilunar valves as the ventricles relax.
